title.en: Let the permutation state drive the puzzle

summary: Hold piece permutation and orientation as the authoritative state and commit exactly one change per completed move.
objective: Give a twisty puzzle a state model that stays exact through animation, interruption and repeated play.
applies_when: A puzzle with movable pieces animates its moves.
Moves can be queued, interrupted or triggered by direct manipulation.
Solved detection, move counting or a scramble is part of the scene.
intent_signals: the cube drifts out of alignment
example_prompts: Build a cube where fast turns never corrupt the state.
Show the current permutation as I turn.
negative_signals: Free-form sculpture or decoration that resembles a puzzle.
not_for: Free-form sculpture or decoration that resembles a puzzle.

principles: The puzzle is a discrete object. Its state is which piece is in which position and how each is oriented, and everything else, including the rendered transforms, is derived from that.

Animation is a display of a transition, not the transition itself. If the state is updated gradually, an interrupted or overlapping animation leaves the puzzle in a position that corresponds to no legal state.
Committing exactly once per move keeps move counting, solved detection and history exact regardless of animation speed or frame drops.
Rebuilding the rendered pose from the state after each commit removes accumulated floating-point drift, which otherwise appears as a slowly disintegrating puzzle.
implementation: Represent the state as a permutation of piece identities plus an orientation value per piece, and derive all transforms from it.

Apply each move to the model exactly once and display the transition around it. Committing when the animation completes, with a temporary visual transform over the pre-move state, and committing at the start, with a display transition that lags the model, are both valid; what matters is exactly one model transition per move and a declared policy for interruption.
Define the policy for overlapping input explicitly: queue, reject or fast-forward, and apply it consistently.
Snap the rendered pose to the exact state after each commit rather than accumulating rotations.

Derive solved detection from the state, and derive the move count from the committed move history rather than from the arrangement: the solved arrangement is reached by zero turns and also by four identical quarter turns, which are different counts.
observable_checks: Issue rapid overlapping turns and confirm the state remains a valid permutation, that each accepted move produced exactly one model transition, and that the move count matches the committed history under the declared interruption policy.
Interrupt an animation partway and confirm the puzzle either completes or cancels the move cleanly with no half-applied state.
Perform a long sequence and confirm the pieces remain exactly aligned rather than drifting.
Reach the solved state by an unusual route and confirm detection fires from the state.

creative_affordances: Puzzle geometry, materials, animation curves and effects are entirely free above this state contract.
Invented puzzle mechanisms work the same way once their legal move set is defined.
known_limits: Authored state-model guidance; no runtime puzzle has been exercised for this record.
It does not provide a solver or an optimal-move claim.
